tob-10790: Hereward Carrington, better known as a writer on psychic phenomena, turns his popularizing pen to chemistry in this beginner’s primer. He explains atoms, elements, and basic reactions in plain language for the general reader. The book is a time capsule of how the science was taught to laypeople in the early twentieth century.
tob-11490: Brother Lawrence was a seventeenth-century Carmelite lay brother who washed dishes in a Paris monastery — and became famous for doing it in constant conversation with God. His conversations and letters teach that prayer is not a task for church hours but a habit of the heart, possible anywhere. This little book has comforted busy believers for three centuries.
tob-0190: Sir Edwin Arnold’s Song Celestial pours the Bhagavad Gita into rolling English verse, from Arjuna’s despair on the field to Krishna’s crowning vision. The Victorian poet kept the Gita’s eighteen books and its climb from doubt to light. His rendering bore India’s beloved scripture into countless English homes.
tob-4090: Sacred Books of the East volume sixteen strings Legge’s Confucian renderings — the Yi King and fellow ground-books. His learned gear and careful notes made Chinese thought open to the Victorian West. The volume stays a cornerstone of English China-study.
tob-4190: Arthur Ryder’s 1925 Panchatantra gives the classic Sanskrit beast-fables — five books of tales teaching niti, the rede of getting on. His sparkling Englishing is the beloved version. The stories have gladdened readers two thousand years, from Indian courts to latter-day nurseries.
tob-4290: Hans Sloane’s Jamaica Voyage — 1707 — sets down his faring as the Duke of Albemarle’s leech, listing the isle’s plants, beasts, and folk. The great herb-man’s toil seeded the British wonder-house. His gatherings became the Museum’s founding stock. It stays a landmark of settle-land nature-lore.
cia-0000105890: Dated April 1965, this report examines how President Sukarno maneuvered to keep Indonesia's rival power blocs — the army, the communists, and religious groups — in balance. Sukarno's balancing act was the center of Indonesian politics, and American analysts studied every shift. Within months the balance would collapse into violence.
cia-0000107290: A June 1991 report bluntly titled: no American soldiers in Cambodia. As MIA investigators chased leads across Southeast Asia, ruling places out mattered as much as following leads in. The document is a flat denial preserved in the archive — one small cleared square on a large, painful map.
cia-0000108490: An estimated January 1983 document, title deleted, on the arrest of American and Spanish citizens in Guatemala. Foreigners swept up in the civil war's security dragnet became diplomatic problems overnight. The censored title leaves the full story untold, but the fragment confirms Washington was watching its people abroad.
cia-0000115490: An interagency intelligence memorandum on the situation in Nicaragua, estimated to date from August 1981. The Sandinistas held power, the Contras were organizing, and Washington was choosing sides. The memo captures the intelligence community briefing policymakers at the start of a conflict that would consume the decade.
cia-0000118690: A February 1977 regional and political analysis of Latin America. The Carter years brought a new lens — human rights — to a continent of dictators. The document surveys the hemisphere as the old Cold War certainties began to shift.
cia-0000119590: An estimated January 1964 document on an impending announcement of a drastic austerity program — the truncated title hides the country. Belt-tightening by governments often foreshadowed unrest. The entry shows the CIA watching economic pain as a predictor of political trouble.
cia-0000126890: A situation report as of 1:00 PM local time on February 17, 1968 — the archive gives no theater, but the date screams Tet Offensive. Timestamped sitreps were the Vietnam War's pulse. The entry is one heartbeat in the offensive's long aftermath.
cia-0000132290: Situation Report 599 on Iraqi political developments — the truncated title withholds the details. One report short of six hundred, the series chronicled Baghdad's politics under bombardment. The entry is the regime's inner life, glimpsed through the bombing.
cia-0000132590: A September 1960 report: Yugoslavia failing to win Cuban friendship. Tito's courtship of Havana fell short — Castro chose Moscow. The document is the failure: the maverick, rebuffed.
cia-0000135890: A 1954 planning document — subject deleted — with an attached briefing of another deleted person, the garbled title suggests. The plans, layered. The entry is the planning: the briefings, stacked — the names, removed.
cia-0000136290: A 1954 cable from LINCOLN recommending urgent steps to be taken on the United Nations — the truncated title cuts off the matter. The UN front needed action. The document is the recommendation: the steps, urged.
cia-0000136990: A 1954 cable to the senior representative in Guatemala City requesting LINCOLN provide Guatemala with L-something — the truncated title cuts off the noun. The aid, requested. The entry is the provision: the item, unspecified.
cia-0000139490: A 1953 report on prisoner of war camps in North Korea. The camps, surveyed. The document is the geography: the captivity, mapped.
un-sc-res-190: Security Council Resolution 190, cataloged with the year 1963 — the numbering suggests 1964, a small inconsistency. The designation is kept; the date is questioned.
un-sc-res-390: Security Council Resolution 390, cataloged with the year 1923 — more than two decades before the Council existed, an impossible date. The designation is preserved; the year is wrong. The entry is the error: the number, kept — the date, impossible.
un-sc-res-1590: Security Council Resolution 1590, cataloged with the year 1990 — though the well-known Sudan mission resolution of that number belongs to 2005, a deep mismatch. The designation is kept; the date is doubted — and the subject is left to the text.
un-sc-res-1790: Security Council Resolution 1790, adopted in December 2007 — the Iraq force extension, prolonging the multinational force's mandate for a final year. The occupation's legal clock kept ticking. The resolution is the extension: the mandate, prolonged.
un-sc-res-1990: Security Council Resolution 1990, adopted in June 2011 — the Abyei resolution, creating the UN Interim Security Force for the disputed Sudan-South Sudan border region. The peacekeepers deployed to the fault line. The resolution is the force: the disputed zone, guarded.
cia-0000132490: A 1960 CIA file titled simply Cuba, numbered 0000132490. The revolution's second year. The entry is the dossier: the island, documented.
cia-0000135690: A 1960 CIA file of Spanish-text 2506 Brigade documents — number 0000135690. The Spanish papers accumulated. The entry is the accumulation: the papers, growing.
un-sc-res-1090: Security Council Resolution 1090, cataloged with the year 1090 — the year field echoes the number, plainly garbage; the real 1090 belongs to 1996. The designation is kept; the date is discarded.
stubbe-peeter-werewolf-1590: The Damnable Life and Death of One Stubbe Peeter, a 1590 pamphlet — the sensational English account of Peter Stumpp, the German farmer executed as a werewolf, sorcerer, and murderer. True crime meets monster tale at the dawn of print. The pamphlet is the sensation: the werewolf, reported.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d90: The ambassador in the United Kingdom, Winant, to the President, November 2 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 90. London's embassy reported. The cable is the embassy's: Winant, informing.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d190: The ambassador in the Soviet Union, Harriman, to the President, November 4 — the truncated title cuts off the year — Document 190. Moscow's embassy reported too. The cable is the parallel: two embassies, one day.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d290: A memorandum by the British Chiefs of Staff, November 23, 1943 — Document 290. The British planners' paper. The memo is the planners': the chiefs, British.
frus-1943-cairo-tehran-d390: The minister in Iran, Dreyfus, to the president's special representative — the truncated title cuts off the rest — Document 390. Tehran's legation wrote the envoy. The cable is the legation's: Dreyfus, informing.
arxiv-2605-08890: Three atoms arranged just so can act as an antenna for light, and the geometry decides how strongly light and matter talk. Linsa G. J, Pushpender Singh, Rohit Dhir, and M. Ameen Poyli tune that interaction through symmetry, resolving how the trimer's shape controls its optical response. The 2026 paper is nanophotonics: antennas built from atoms.
arxiv-2605-09290: Neural architecture search hunts good network designs, and predictors guess performance without full training. Liping Deng and MingQing Xiao move from regression to inference: meta-learning predictors that know their uncertainty. The 2026 paper makes architecture search smarter about what it does not know.
arxiv-2605-09490: LLM reasoning intermediates do not all deserve expensive high-bandwidth memory — some thoughts matter more than others. Aojie Yuan, Tianqi Shen, and Dajun Zhang build a semantics-aware memory hierarchy: important thoughts get the fast memory. The 2026 paper is systems research for cheaper, smarter reasoning.
arxiv-2605-10090: In-memory vector approximate nearest neighbor search on multi-core CPUs, orchestrated at CCD level with load awareness. Yuchen Huang, Baiteng Ma, Yiping Sun, and colleagues develop the orchestration. The 2026 paper is vector search tuned to the silicon. It orchestrates threads for maximum speed.
plos-pone-0003390: Nutrition scientists connected a vitamin-like balance to cancer defense in this 2008 mouse study. The typical Western diet skimps on methyl nutrients that feed the body's methylation chemistry. Mice fed a methyl-balanced diet gained protection against cancer, but only when the RIZ1 gene was intact, showing that diet's shield works through a specific genetic gatekeeper.
plos-pone-0003490: Geneticists flagged a new multiple-sclerosis suspect region in this 2008 study. Scanning the genomes of 500 patients with pooled DNA, they identified a risk locus at chromosome 13q31.3, beyond the well-known HLA immune genes. The finding adds a fresh address to the genetic map of this chronic demyelinating disease.
plos-pone-0003590: Stress researchers hunted blood markers of burnout in women in this 2009 paper. Prolonged psychosocial stress is usually measured by questionnaire, so the team measured plasma compounds seeking biochemical signatures for screening and early intervention. Objective markers could move stress detection from self-report to the lab bench.
plos-pone-0003690: In 2008, Etzel, Gazzola, and Keysers put simulation theory to a brain-scan test. If we understand others' actions by mirroring them in our own motor system, then seeing and doing should share neural codes. Their cross-modal decoding of fMRI data tested that shared code directly, weighing a big idea about social minds.
plos-pone-0003790: Magalhaes, Sizemore, and Ahmed tested a one-two punch against TB in monkeys in this 2008 paper. Recombinant BCG primed the immune system, and an adenovirus boost strengthened the T-cell response in rhesus macaques. The prime-boost combo aims to make TB protection stronger, broader, and longer-lasting.
plos-pone-0003890: Working in 2008, a team linked a brain chemical to reading minds. Prefrontal glutamate levels tracked with mental perspective-taking, the ability to see through others' eyes. The correlation ties the brain's main excitatory signal to the core of social understanding.
plos-pone-0003990: In 2008, Osipova, Hermes, and Jensen found brain rhythms riding each other. Gamma-band power locked to the phase of alpha activity in the back of the head. The cross-frequency coupling shows brain rhythms coordinating across their different scales. The finding adds a new layer to how brain oscillations organize thought.
plos-pone-0004090: In 2008, Pfister, Ma, and Morrison found sibling enzymes at war in the brain. SIRT1 protected neurons, while other sirtuins pushed the opposite way. Its defense of nerve cells did not need its enzyme activity. The family split complicates anti-aging hopes for sirtuins.
plos-pone-0004190: In 2009, Bondar, Boyarskikh, and Kovalenko read aggression in mouse brains. Repeated fighting shifted Th, Dat1, Snca, and Bdnf gene activity in the VTA. The reward circuit's genes tracked each violent experience. The molecular trace links aggression to altered brain chemistry.
plos-pone-0004290: In 2009, Weber, Kula-Eversole, and Pyza found fly eyes breathing with the daily clock. Circadian rhythms reshaped dendrites in the fly visual system daily. Lamina neurons and glia swelled and shrank on schedule. The clockwork shows the brain remaking itself nightly.
plos-pone-0355690: Security cameras record endless hours that nobody watches — until something goes wrong. This paper builds a deep-learning system that scans surveillance footage and flags unusual human activity, like fighting or falling, by learning what normal looks like across space and time. The goal is software that alerts a human operator only when something genuinely needs attention.
plos-pone-0357590: Quantum computers will shred today’s encryption — and 6G networks must be ready before they arrive. QShield-ZTN is a quantum-resilient, standards-compliant secure orchestration model for autonomous 6G zero-touch networks. The model bakes post-quantum safety into the communication networks of the future.
plos-pone-0358190: Invoice seals prove documents are genuine — and forgers fake them constantly. ISD-YOLO is a lightweight, efficient feature extraction network built for invoice seal detection. The model automates fraud detection in paperwork, flagging suspicious seals faster than any human clerk could.
plos-pone-0357490: Fitting rigid gas permeable contact lenses demands hands-on practice — ideally not on live patients first. This pilot study integrated 3D-printed sclero-corneal eye models into RGP lens training. The printed eyes give trainees realistic, repeatable practice before they touch a real cornea.
plos-pone-0357290: Do insect-eating animals absorb the hormones from their prey? This paper asked whether insect food-derived ecdysteroids — arthropod molting hormones — appear in the blood of waterfowl, predatory birds, carnivorous mammals, and primates. The answer traces a fascinating thread of food-chain chemistry.
plos-pone-0356790: Greater spear-nosed bats organize into sex-biased social groups — and behavior tells them apart. This paper showed affiliative and agonistic interactions distinguish the groups. The bat sociology reveals a surprisingly structured social world in the roost’s darkness.
plos-pone-0357090: Erbil’s explosive growth follows corridors — and a graph neural network can read them. This paper used a graph convolutional network to model corridor-based urban transformation, revealing spatial coherence in land-use change. The model maps how the Kurdish capital is really growing.
plos-pone-0356990: Online stores learn what goes with what from association rules — but most of those rules are redundant noise. This paper moved from redundant association rules to clean product networks using a scalable confidence-improvement pruning method plus a Maximum Spanning Tree approach. The pruned networks reveal genuine product relationships, giving retailers recommendation graphs they can actually trust and compute at scale.
plos-pone-0356690: Acute intermittent fasting affects women’s mood, hunger, sleep, and diet satisfaction — but how do different protocols compare? This crossover experimental study compared them head-to-head in females. The within-person design delivers unusually trustworthy answers about fasting’s real effects.
plos-pone-0356490: Lipoprotein(a) — a potent cardiovascular risk factor — is understudied in Africa. This systematic review mapped its burden across the continent. The synthesis reveals a hidden epidemic of Lp(a)-driven heart risk that African health systems must start screening for.
plos-pone-0355290: Mentorship shapes science careers — but its value depends on institutional context. This paper drew insights from biology and biomedical science undergraduates at two different institutions. Comparing their experiences reveals what makes mentoring work across settings — and what universities must fix to keep talented students in science.
plos-pone-0356390: Chinese college students learning English as a second language engage — or disengage — for complex reasons. This paper examined classroom engagement through perceived teacher support, value beliefs, and self-monitoring. The findings reveal which levers teachers can actually pull to keep students invested in the hard work of mastering another tongue.
plos-pone-0355390: Orthokeratology lenses — worn overnight to reshape the cornea — promise myopia control for teens. This paper measured one-year effects on objective visual quality and corneal densitometry in myopic adolescents. The detailed ocular data help eye doctors weigh the benefits against the risks of overnight lens wear.
plos-pone-0353190: Shoppers pay more for meat with sustainability labels — but how much more? This paper measured the price premiums for labeled meat products. The quantified premiums tell producers whether sustainable practices pay — and tell policymakers whether labels genuinely shift markets.
plos-pone-0353990: Happiness makes distant ideas feel closer — but only in your mother tongue. This paper showed positive mood enhances accessibility of unrelated concepts in the first language but not in a foreign language. The findings reveal that emotion’s cognitive effects are language-specific — a subtle twist with implications for bilingual life.
plos-pone-0353490: Gen Z shops in phygital spaces — blending physical and digital retail. This paper unlocked their engagement with a multi-mediated customer experience model. The findings tell retailers how to design hybrid experiences that resonate with the generation that never knew a purely physical store.
europmc-pmc2836990: Muscles grow dramatically after birth, and this 2010 paper watches the process in mice. The authors track the dynamics of muscle fiber growth during postnatal development. Their detailed timeline shows how fibers lengthen and mature. The baseline data helps researchers spot what goes wrong in muscle diseases.
europmc-pmc2847190: Bees brave both gut bugs and field sprays at once, and this 2010 paper shows the pair hits worse than each alone. The team proves Nosema spores plus a neonicotinoid sap bee vigor. Their caged trials bare a one-two punch. The find snarled the debate on what's felling bees.
europmc-pmc2851690: Not all immune cells near a tumor aid the tumor; some fight it. This 2010 lung cancer study finds the M1 form of tumor-linked macrophages tracks with longer life in non-small cell cases. The team tied cell form to fate. The split urged treatments that back the fighting form.
europmc-pmc2866690: Flame retardants called PBDEs reach the womb, and this 2010 study tracks the kids. The authors link prenatal PBDE exposure to poorer neurodevelopment. Their findings joined a chorus on these chemicals and young brains. The study fed the push to phase PBDEs out.
europmc-pmc2891790: PDZ domains are the cell's Velcro, small parts that grip partner proteins. This 2010 review covers how they are built, how they pick partners, and how cells tweak them. The authors map a gripping module found all over the cell. Their roundup aids drug makers aiming at these grips.
europmc-pmc2912890: Genomes are full of repeats, and this 2010 paper sorts them. The authors group look-alike repeats with graph math in new gene-read data. Their method tames the repeat jungle that chokes assemblers. Their tool aided genome building for tricky species.
europmc-pmc2935890: B vitamins might slow brain shrinkage in early memory loss. This 2010 randomized trial finds B vitamins that lower homocysteine slow the pace of brain shrinkage in mild cognitive impairment. The authors' result offers a cheap, safe hope. Their trial spurred a wave of nutrition-brain research.
europmc-pmc3002190: Chemicals need hormone screening at scale. This 2010 paper uses the ToxCast program to flag chemicals that meddle with hormones. The authors rank the worst suspects. Their work aids chemical safety rules. Regulators test thousands of compounds this way. The worst offenders face bans or limits.
europmc-pmc3023790: Plant stress genes answer to WRKY regulators. This 2010 paper shows three WRKY proteins steer the mustard plant's drought and stress replies. The authors reveal the control trio. Their work aids stress-proof crops. The trio also brakes overeager defenses. Breeders stack these switches in wheat.
europmc-pmc3042390: Heavy phone use may fray young minds. This 2011 Swedish study links mobile phone use to stress, sleep disturbances, and depression symptoms in young adults. The authors' prospective cohort warns of overload. Their work fueled digital-wellness debates. Late-night scrolling wrecked sleep most.
europmc-pmc3042690: Germs can eat oil spills. This 2011 review covers microbes that digest petroleum pollutants. The authors survey the hungry germs. Their overview guides spill cleanup. Some germs feast only on crude oil. Beaches recover faster with germ help. The review lists the champion degraders.
europmc-pmc3047790: Steroid drugs calm inflammation, and this 2011 review explains how. The authors detail how glucocorticoids douse immune fires. Their overview maps the mechanisms. The review guides doctors. The drugs save lives but exact a toll. Bone loss and weight gain shadow long use.
europmc-pmc3098090: DNA snippets got placed on trees fast. This 2010 paper brings pplacer, a tool that slots sequences onto family trees. The authors' program handles huge microbiomes. Their software spread through labs. Gut surveys place millions of reads daily. The math runs in linear time.
europmc-pmc6509190: The bacteria living in our gut talk to the brain through a two-way connection scientists are still decoding. This study found that Alzheimer's patients carry gut microbes linked to a broken anti-inflammatory defense called the P-glycoprotein pathway. The finding adds weight to the idea that infections and chronic inflammation help drive the disease, and that the gut could become a target for new treatments.
europmc-pmc6512290: After colon cancer surgery, tiny traces of tumor DNA floating in the blood can reveal whether cancer remains. This study used extremely sensitive sequencing to hunt for those traces in patients with early-stage colorectal cancer. The test could help doctors decide who needs extra chemotherapy after surgery and who can safely skip it.
europmc-pmc6548990: Macrophages live or die by signals through two receptors - TNFR1 and TNFR2 - that read the same immune messenger, TNF, with opposite outcomes. This review untangles how the pair balances macrophage survival against programmed death. Getting the balance right matters: it decides whether these frontline defenders hold the line or fall in infection and inflammation.
europmc-pmc6567490: Gut microbes feast on what we cannot digest - fiber, resistant starch, leftover protein - and their fermentation leftovers shape our health. This review catalogs the major by-products (short-chain fatty acids and friends) and their effects, from gut lining to brain. Understanding microbial metabolism turns 'eat your fiber' into precise science.
europmc-pmc6585590: Recovery coaches with lived addiction experience - peers, not professionals - are joining treatment teams in growing numbers. This systematic review asks whether peer recovery support actually helps people with substance use disorder stay the course. The evidence is promising but patchy, pointing to where peer programs work best and what good training looks like.
europmc-pmc6604390: CRISPR diagnostics keep getting sharper: CDetection uses the Cas12b enzyme to spot DNA with sub-attomolar sensitivity - a few molecules in a sea - while telling single-letter differences apart. The method promises field-ready tests that catch pathogens or mutations with lab-grade precision from tiny samples.
europmc-pmc6714090: Liver cancer thrives by bribing the immune system into silence. This review surveys the immunosuppressive tumor microenvironment of hepatocellular carcinoma: the cells and signals that shield the tumor. Understanding the shield is the first step to cracking it - and making immunotherapy work where it currently falters.
europmc-pmc6717890: Microglia were once cast as a single character - the brain's janitor. This review reveals a diverse cast: distinct microglial subtypes with different jobs across development, adulthood, and disease. The community portrait replaces the lone-janitor myth with a nuanced ensemble.
europmc-pmc6761190: CAR-T therapy is powerful but toxic - the engineered cells can rage out of control. This study found their exosomes pack the punch without the peril: CAR exosomes from effector CAR-T cells kill tumors with low toxicity. The cell-free vesicles could deliver CAR power more safely.
europmc-pmc6769590: Selenium is a trace mineral with an outsized job: building selenoproteins that manage oxidative stress. This review examines how selenium status shapes viral infections - the ROS burst viruses trigger and the defenses selenoproteins mount. The mineral's antiviral angle deserves more attention.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-990: Homeland Security was buying blind in spots, GAO's 2007 report says — big service deals signed with thin homework on what the money bought. The findings press the department to size up its buys and watch its vendors. For an agency built at sprint speed, the report demands grown-up shopping habits.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-290: The rental-aid rulebook was going stale in 2007 — GAO's report says housing officials should update the policies for project-based help. The findings demand a full refresh. The report's logic: the housing market moved on, so the manual must move too.
gao-gaoreports-gao-07-90: The personnel agency was learning hard lessons in 2007, and GAO's report distills what OPM had learned about leading human capital reform. The findings share the wisdom. The report shows the government's HR shop studying its own homework. The lessons had to stick.
openalex-w7207688590: The vegetables at open-air markets can carry more than vitamins. This study tested produce sold at street fairs and markets in Tres Rios and Paraiba do Sul, Rio de Janeiro, for parasites, signs of fecal contamination, and other microscopic organisms. The authors measured how widespread the problem is and what the sanitary indicators show. A public-health wake-up call about washing produce, and about sanitation in the food chain.
openalex-w7204272490: The old school prized sameness; today's school must prize difference. This article studies the shift from the uniform modern school to a diverse contemporary one, and what it demands of teaching and learning. The authors focus on Brazil's cultural mix and historic inequalities. A philosophy-of-education piece on schooling built for many, not one.
openalex-w7165480890: Shine light on a quantum dot and electrons can hop with a photon's help. This theoretical paper studies photon-assisted tunneling in paired quantum dots, tiny electron traps, solving the time-dependent quantum equations. The authors build the math from one dot to two. Fundamental physics of light nudging electricity at the nanoscale.
openalex-w7153077790: Some germs shrug off our strongest drugs, and Acinetobacter baumannii ranks among the worst. This lab study tested sulbactam-based mixes on its resistant strains. The team also probed how the resistance works. A germ study arming doctors against a superbug.
pmc-13521290: A 2026 plant biology review of the PHO1 protein family, which moves phosphate out of plant cells and roots. The authors cover its core role in phosphorus nutrition and newer discoveries of other jobs these proteins do. Since phosphorus is essential for crops, the review matters for agriculture and plant science.
pmc-13459190: A 2026 study redesigning how hand therapy using virtual reality gets evaluated — this time with patients as co-designers. Rather than imposing metrics from above, the authors worked with consumers to define what engagement really means in VR rehab. The result is an evaluation framework built around what matters to the people doing the therapy.
pmc-13458390: This 2026 molecular biology paper shows that menin, a known tumor suppressor protein, acts as a scaffold that organizes homologous recombination repair — the cell's high-fidelity method for fixing broken DNA. By holding the repair machinery together, menin helps prevent the mutations that lead to cancer. The finding connects a cancer gene to the nuts and bolts of genome maintenance.
pmc-13455090: This 2026 review surveys proteomic biomarker discovery in breast cancer — hunting for protein signatures in blood or tissue that flag the disease, predict outcomes, or guide therapy. The authors cover recent advances, persistent challenges, and how close these markers are to the clinic. It is a field guide to the protein side of cancer detection.
pmc-13438190: A 2026 Alzheimer's study showing that blood-based p-tau217 can detect Alzheimer's co-pathology in patients with cerebral amyloid angiopathy — a vessel disease of the brain — comparing it against spinal fluid biomarkers in the ANGMAR cohort. A blood test that sorts out mixed pathology would simplify diagnosis considerably.
pmc-13420190: This 2026 cross-sectional study surveyed professional values, work environment, and job satisfaction among critical care nurses in Palestine. ICU nursing under occupation and resource strain is uniquely demanding. The descriptive data give policymakers a baseline for supporting this workforce.
pmc-13380890: A 2026 study linking COVID-19 vaccine regret and distrust of the healthcare system to future vaccine intentions. Regret and distrust predict refusal more than facts predict acceptance. The findings argue that rebuilding trust, not just informing, is the vaccination challenge.
pmc-13305690: A 2026 psychiatry paper asking whether prediction of early-onset mania and hypomania in the community can be improved. Catching bipolar disorder before the first full episode changes the prognosis. The study tests what predictive signals actually work.
pmc-13553590: A 2026 data paper presenting a temporally harmonized gridded building-stock dataset for the Global South, 2016–2023. Buildings data underpin disaster and climate planning. The harmonized dataset is a public resource.
pmc-13481590: A 2026 study analyzing prognostic factors for CD19 CAR-T therapy followed by stem cell transplant in relapsed/refractory B-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia. The combination sequence needs optimization. The factor analysis guides it.
pmc-13452290: This 2026 case report localized a lumbar microspur-related ventral CSF leak using digital subtraction myelography. The tiny bone spur caused the spinal fluid leak. The imaging localization solved it.
pmc-13423190: A 2026 NLP paper on a parallel dual-stream state-space module for reliable and efficient biomedical relation extraction. Mining relationships from medical text needs speed and accuracy. The module is the advance.
pmc-13616090: This 2026 data paper described SCL2205 — a protein sequence-based spatial modeling dataset for the protein language model frontier. The dataset trains the next generation of protein AI. The scale is the selling point.
pmc-13530590: This 2026 conference poster explored improving rotator cuff repair with tissue engineering and biotherapeutics. The biologics-enhanced repair is the frontier. The poster surveys the approaches.
pmc-13448290: This 2026 conference abstract (TLSB-33) reported patterns of CNS progression and outcomes in metastatic breast cancer patients treated with sacituzumab govitecan. The antibody-drug conjugate's brain effects were tracked. The abstract gives the multicenter data.
pmc-13504290: In this 2026 biophysics paper, imaging and mechanism of DNA-DNA recognition mediated by divalent ions were studied. The ions bridged the helices. The mechanism is the insight.
pmc-13495090: In this 2026 qualitative paper, a biographical-narrative toolkit traced anxious lives — anxieties and coping strategies across three central and eastern European countries. The narratives revealed coping. The toolkit is the method.
pmc-13490890: A 2026 mycology paper on enzymatic activity of clinical and environmental Aspergillus flavus isolates. The enzyme profiles were compared. The activity patterns characterize the fungus.
pmc-13470590: In this 2026 prospective case series, infected non-union of long bones was managed with antibiotic cement-coated intramedullary nails. The coated nails delivered local antibiotics. The series is the evidence.
pmc-13473990: A 2026 paper on multi-model ensembles in ecosystem modeling — challenges and best practices for decision-making. The ensemble approach was examined. The best practices guide modelers.
pmc-13431790: A 2026 review on intron retention in health and amyotrophic lateral sclerosis. The splicing phenomenon's disease role was surveyed. The review is the synthesis.
pmc-13421790: This 2026 paper, "Dividends and Disconnects," involved public and stakeholder groups in developing a modeling study exploring income policy and health. The participatory modeling was the approach. The involvement is the democratic element.
pmc-13401090: A 2026 comparative dose and image quality assessment of a portable multi-modality extremity imaging system for austere environments. The field-ready imager was tested. The assessment serves military and disaster medicine.
pmc-13439690: A 2026 software paper introducing VIDEO — visual integration of Drosophila enhancer organization, a tool integrating chromatin accessibility and transcription factor data (the title is truncated). The fly enhancer browser is the tool. The integration is the feature.
pmc-13518090: In this 2026 transethnic GWAS, novel immune-related susceptibility loci for pediatric steroid-sensitive nephrotic syndrome were identified (the title is truncated). The childhood kidney disease's genetics were mapped. The loci are the discovery.
pmc-13431990: A 2026 Portuguese-language paper, "Between setbacks and advances," tracing the trajectory of food insecurity in Black households in Brazil from 2013 to 2023. The racial food security gap was charted. The trajectory is the policy evidence.
pmc-13620190: This 2026 paper used unsupervised clustering of intradialytic blood pressure patterns and their associations with body composition in chronic hemodialysis patients (the title is truncated). The dialysis blood pressure patterns were clustered. The associations are the finding.
pmc-13464790: In this 2026 review, "Beyond Ablation," immune responses across focused ultrasound modalities were examined. The ultrasound's immune effects were surveyed. The review is the immuno-oncology outlook.
pmc-13462990: This 2026 paper explored the link between body physiology and cognition — the role of the brain and aging. The body-mind connection was examined. The exploring is the synthesis.
pmc-13446490: A 2026 education paper: a model for crystallography engagement with early elementary school children, with activities and book development. The young scientists were engaged. The model serves outreach.
pmc-13592790: A 2026 paper on pulmonary hypertension in patients with moderate to severe hypersensitivity pneumonitis. The lung disease's vascular complication was profiled. The paper informs pulmonology.
arxiv-2606-16090: Anyons are exotic quantum particles whose strange exchange behavior could power new kinds of computation. This paper asks whether they can also enhance quantum machine learning — using anyonic systems to run learning algorithms. It is a theoretical proposal at the intersection of quantum computing and AI, aimed at researchers in both fields.
arxiv-2606-16490: Two robots carrying a table must move as one — their policies are coupled. This paper teaches such collaboration through "sequential asymmetric imitation": one robot learns first, then the second learns to complement it. The approach gives robotics researchers a practical way to train robot teams on shared physical tasks.
arxiv-2606-16590: Babies move spontaneously long before they can walk, and those early movements reveal how motor control develops. This paper studies infant spontaneous movements — the kicks, waves, and wiggles of early life — likely with computational analysis of motion data. It targets developmental researchers and roboticists learning from human motor development.
arxiv-2606-16690: Robots learn manipulation in "action chunks" — bursts of motion — and things go wrong mid-chunk. PATCH monitors for innovation (surprises) within those chunks using action-chunk-conditioned latent patches, catching failures early. It targets robotics researchers making learned manipulation safer and more reliable.
arxiv-2606-16890: Medical AI that chains many reasoning steps can fail in sneaky ways. This paper finds that compositional reasoning depth predicts clinical AI failure — with empirical evidence. It is a cautionary study for medical AI safety. Longer chains mean bigger risks here.
